name: Gyrodrillmatic Excavationators
summary: In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent prepares a fleet of tunneling machines for Dun Morogh. Short on parts, she sends you into Gnomeregan to salvage them from rogue automatons.

sections.title: A Fleet in Need of Guts
sections.body: In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent prepares a fleet of gyrodrillmatic excavationators for Dun Morogh. Gnomish engineers there support their displaced kin, and Shoni's machines are meant to carry people and supplies underground. The massive rigs cannot work without the mechanical parts she still lacks.

sections.title: Salvage in the Fallen City
sections.body: Gnomeregan was the source of gnomish high technology, and its ruined halls and surrounding tunnels still hold machines worth salvaging. Malfunctioning defense bots, mechanical sentries, and clockwork laborers roam unchecked. Shoni sends you into the fallen city to gather two dozen bundles of robo-mechanical guts and bring them back to human lands.

sections.title: A Monumental Undertaking
sections.body: Two dozen bundles of mechanical guts provide enough scrap to repair one excavationator. Shoni still has nearly four hundred machines to prepare, so mass subterranean transport remains a slow undertaking. Each functioning machine is a small step toward regaining ground lost in Gnomeregan's fall.

faq.answer: A gyrodrillmatic excavationator is a heavy gnomish tunneling rig, also called a mole machine, built for digging and transport underground. Shoni the Shilent is preparing a fleet to move people or supplies to Dun Morogh.
Shoni the Shilent is a gnomish engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Outspoken and demanding, she is preparing hundreds of mechanical diggers.

faq.q: Why does Shoni need parts from Gnomeregan specifically?
faq.answer: Gnomeregan was the source of gnomish high technology, and its fallen halls hold haywire automatons, clockwork servitors, and defensive mechs. With the city's manufacturing supply lines severed, these rogue machines offer compatible gnomish spare parts.

faq.q: Where are the Robo-Mechanical Guts found?
faq.answer: Robo-Mechanical Guts can be salvaged from mechanical sentries, clockwork constructs, and other hostile machines in Gnomeregan's ruined facility and upper tunnel approaches.

faq.q: Does fixing one machine finish Shoni's fleet?
faq.answer: No. Two dozen bundles of mechanical guts repair one drill. Shoni says she still has 398 excavationators left to go.

faq.q: Why is an excavation fleet being prepared for Dun Morogh?
faq.answer: Dun Morogh is the gnomes' ancestral home and the site of their fallen capital. Heavy tunneling rigs can help dig, clear debris, and support work in the snow-covered mountain reaches.

angles.text: As a gnome, every salvaged component brings Shoni's subterranean fleet closer to working order. The dream of reclamation and industrial recovery lives on from Stormwind.
As an engineer, stripping precise clockwork innards from Gnomeregan's fallen servitors offers a practical lesson in gnomish design and heavy machinery repair.
As an Alliance member, supporting gnomish excavation from Stormwind strengthens ties between the human hosts and exiled survivors working to reclaim their heritage.
